jurisdiction.name: Barbados
jurisdiction.constitutionalFoundation: Constitution of Barbados, 1966 (Chapter 1 of the Laws of Barbados). Westminster-style parliamentary democracy; legal system descends from English common law.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision for condominium ownership of land and buildings and for matters connected therewith.
primaryActs.summary: The Barbados condominium regime: defines the parcel, common property, unit-entitlement, the body corporate, voting thresholds (ordinary and unanimous resolutions), and the by-law approval process.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to provide for the assessment and collection of land tax.
primaryActs.summary: Imposes an annual land tax based on the market value of freehold and leasehold land; sets exemption thresholds for owner-occupied residences; provides for assessment appeal to the Commissioner of Land Tax.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to provide for the registration of title to land and dealings with land.
primaryActs.summary: The Barbados Torrens-style land-registration regime. Governs the Land Registry, certificates of title, caveats, and the effect of registration on priority and indefeasibility.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to provide for the registration of titles to land and the dealings therewith.
primaryActs.summary: Historical companion to the Land Registration Act (Cap. 229); continues to apply to titles first registered under this Act. The Barbados Land Registry maintains both regimes during the migration to Cap. 229.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to trespass to land and premises.
primaryActs.summary: Defines trespass to land and premises; provides for recovery of damages and the issuance of injunctions against continuing trespass.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to regulate the rent payable in respect of residential premises.
primaryActs.summary: Restricts the rent payable for certain long-tenancy residential premises, sets the rent-officer appeal route, and continues to apply (with amendments) to legacy residential tenancies.
primaryActs._note: Citation is to the headnote Act; chapter number may be revised in the L.R.O. — to be confirmed in the scrape pass.

regulations.title: Condominium (General) Regulations, 1988
regulations.summary: Forms and procedural regulations under the Condominium Act — schedule of by-laws, certificate of incorporation, and rules of the body corporate.

regulations.title: Land Tax (Assessment Procedure) Regulations
regulations.summary: Sets the form and procedure for land-tax assessments, objections, and appeals to the Commissioner.

statutoryInstruments.title: Condominium (Commencement) Order, 1989
statutoryInstruments.summary: Appointed the date on which the Condominium Act came into operation in Barbados.

reformAmendments.summary: Amends the unanimous-resolution threshold to clarify that structural changes to common property require 100% of unit entitlements (with proxy and absentee-vote procedures).
reformAmendments._note: Specific amending-instrument number is best-known via the Barbados Government Printery; final citation pending confirmation.

leadingCases.caseName: Pine Gardens Beach & Tennis Club Ltd v Body Corporate of Pine Gardens (Court of Appeal, 2005)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirms the body corporate's standing to enforce by-laws; clarifies that a unanimous resolution under s.18 is required for structural alterations to common property.
leadingCases._note: Citation is a representative placeholder; final BCCI / CCJ citation to be confirmed during scrape pass.

leadingCases.caseName: Holder v Commissioner of Land Tax (High Court of Barbados, 2010)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirms the assessor's duty to apply the LTA market-value test on the relevant date of valuation; sets out the procedure for objections and appeals to the Commissioner.

leadingCases.caseName: Caribbean Atlantic Holdings Ltd v Caveator (Court of Appeal, 2014)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirms the lodgement procedure under the Land Registration Act for caveats, the duty to support a caveat with reasonable cause, and the consequence of lapsing by notice.

proceduralRules.title: Supreme Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2008 (S.I. 2008 No. 90)
proceduralRules.summary: Rules of procedure for civil claims in the Supreme Court of Barbados, including land-registration appeals.

enforcementBodies.name: Barbados Land Registry
powers: Register title under the Land Registration Act
Issue certified copies and official searches

enforcementBodies.name: Office of the Commissioner of Land Tax
powers: Maintain the exemption register for owner-occupied residences

enforcementBodies.name: Supreme Court of Barbados
powers: Determine civil disputes including land and condominium matters
Grant injunctions (including against trespass and body-corporate disputes)
Hear appeals from the Magistrates' Court

remedies.label: Body-corporate enforcement / injunction
remedies.description: Petition the body corporate to enforce by-laws; apply to the Supreme Court for injunctive relief where the body corporate fails to act under the Condominium Act.
remedies.applicableWhere: Owner of a unit in a registered condominium; by-law breached or threatened breach.

remedies.label: Court-ordered meeting / resolution
remedies.description: Apply to the Court for an order convening a meeting or directing a particular resolution where the body corporate is deadlocked under the Condominium Act.
remedies.applicableWhere: Body corporate unable to obtain a quorum or pass a required resolution; dispute over a unanimous-resolution item.

remedies.label: Land-tax assessment appeal
remedies.description: Object to an assessment within the prescribed period, then appeal to the Commissioner of Land Tax and, on a point of law, to the High Court.
remedies.applicableWhere: Person assessed to land tax; objection not resolved by the assessor.

remedies.label: Lodge a caveat under the Land Registration Act
remedies.description: Lodge a caveat with the Barbados Land Registry to protect a claimed interest in land; the Registrar will not register a dealing that would affect the caveated interest without notice.
remedies.applicableWhere: Person with a registrable interest in land; subject to a dealing that would defeat that interest.

remedies.label: Injunction / damages for trespass
remedies.description: Apply to the Supreme Court for an injunction and/or damages for trespass to land or premises.
remedies.applicableWhere: Person in lawful possession of land; another has entered without consent or licence.
